brief: Societe Generale's Multi Asset Portfolio raised equities to 58% in September 2026 from 55% in June 2026 and cut government bonds to 12% from 15%, holding cash at 0% and commodities and gold flat at 20%. SG frames the shift as a response to a new world order: nominal GDP and corporate earnings have accelerated together, while the Fed stays behind the curve, with the neutral rate estimated at 3% against a 3.75% Fed funds rate and Kevin Warsh submitting no dot in the September plot. Persistent fiscal deficits reinforce the case: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act widens the deficit with no offset before 2030, and a February 2026 Supreme Court ruling struck down tariffs and wiped out the revenue that had offset it, leaving the US with almost no debt sustainability buffer as rising interest costs offset primary deficit gains. SG also flags hyperscaler capex now peaking higher and later, in mid 2027 rather than end 2026, with post distribution free cash flow turning negative, and links elevated central bank gold buying back to the 2022 freezing of Russian central bank reserves.
